aiOverview.content: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) is a common foaming agent and detergent (surfactant) used in shampoos, soaps, and toothpaste to clean and lather. While effective, it can cause skin and scalp irritation for some users. It is also known as sodium dodecyl sulfate. Other potential meanings for SLS include: Space Launch System: NASA's heavy-lift rocket for deep space missions. Street League Skateboarding: A professional skateboarding tournament series. Scientific Laboratory Supplies: A UK-based supplier of laboratory equipment. Common Uses of Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS): Personal Care Products: Shampoos, body washes, and toothpaste to create foam. Cleaning Agents: Used in household cleaning products due to its high cleansing power. Key Considerations: Irritation: SLS can cause dryness and irritation, particularly for sensitive skin types, and can strip hair of natural oils. SLES vs. SLS: SLES (Sodium Laureth Sulfate) is similar to SLS but is considered milder and gentler. Alternatives: Look for products marked "sulfate-free" or containing alternatives like Sodium Cocoyl Glycinate.
